issues: Whether an unconfirmed, unsettled transfer proposal (with hours/pay terms still 'to be looked at') constitutes a 'reasonable alternative' the claimant was required to pursue before voluntarily leaving under the EI Act's just cause test
Whether just cause for leaving employment can be established where the claimant reasonably believed harassment would continue or recur at the proposed alternative location
Whether an employer's failure to investigate or remedy reported workplace harassment, after complaints to HR and ownership, supports a finding of just cause to leave or constructive dismissal
Whether the employer had an obligation to accommodate the claimant's medical/disability-related restrictions (post-surgery, limited shift capacity) before requiring relocation or a return to work

Whether comments and conduct targeting the claimant's body odour and weight, including gloving/tissue use by coworkers, amount to harassment or discrimination based on disability once the underlying medical cause (abscess) is considered
What standard applies in assessing 'reasonable assurance' that a transfer would resolve the harassment for EI just-cause purposes
key_facts: Coworkers mocked claimant's weight and body odour and used gloves/tissue when interacting with her
Odour was later found to be caused by an undiagnosed abscess
Management spoke to her twice about the odour due to client complaints, before the medical cause was known
She reported harassment to HR and the owner; no corrective action was taken
She went on medical leave, during which she also had ankle surgery
Employer proposed transfer to a second site away from the harassing coworkers
She objected due to longer/costlier commute and inability to manage full shifts while recovering from surgery
Employer said it would 'look at' part-time hours and extra pay requests but nothing was finalized before she resigned
She resigned before the transfer terms were settled, citing distrust of the employer and belief harassment would follow her
EI claim was denied at initial level and first-level appeal on the basis the transfer was a reasonable alternative to quitting
causes_of_action: Disqualification from EI benefits for voluntarily leaving employment without just cause (s. 29-30 EI Act)
Whether reasonable alternatives to leaving existed under s. 29(c) EI Act
Constructive dismissal arising from workplace harassment and failure to address complaints
candidate_statutes: Occupational Health and Safety Act (Ontario) - workplace harassment provisions

reasonable alternative to leaving employment EI Act s.29
